text.paragraph: New patient visit at her own request for binge eating and vomiting: eating-disorder assessment, medical risk assessment, low potassium, mood, and safety planning. Concerns: She wants to stop the cycle of bingeing and vomiting, which she has kept secret and feels ashamed of; She has felt low, tired, and hopeless for some weeks; She is worried about her teeth and the swelling of her cheeks. [S]

list.item: Bulimia nervosa, severe: recurrent binge eating, each time with self-induced vomiting, averaging about ten episodes a week for about three years, hidden from everyone; self-worth tied closely to body shape and weight; no laxatives, diuretics, diet pills, or excessive exercise. SCOFF 4 of 5; EDE-Q global score 3.9. Findings: bilateral parotid enlargement, enamel erosion on the inner surfaces of the upper front teeth, calluses on the backs of two knuckles of the right hand, a pulse rise of 22 per minute on standing, low potassium and chloride with a raised bicarbonate, and a raised amylase; BMI 19.3. Synthetic modern episode linked to her own public account of bulimia: active, confirmed [S]
Hypokalemia (potassium 3.1 mmol/L) with low chloride and metabolic alkalosis from repeated vomiting; QTc 452 ms; no palpitations, weakness, or fainting: resolved, confirmed [S]

Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate: about two months of low mood, tiredness, poor sleep, and feeling worthless and hopeless, with little pleasure in things she used to enjoy; PHQ-9 14 with item 9 scored 0; an earlier episode of depression after childbirth. Synthetic modern episode linked to her own public account of depression: active, confirmed [S]

tr.td: New patient visit at her own request for binge eating and vomiting: eating-disorder assessment, medical risk assessment, low potassium, mood, and safety planning
One-week review: potassium recheck and eating disorders psychiatry consultation
Five-week review: potassium and ECG on fluoxetine 60 mg, CBT-E progress, mood, and safety
Three-month review: binge and purge frequency, electrolytes, dental care, mood, and safety
End-of-treatment review after 20 weeks of CBT-E: remission, relapse prevention, and continuing fluoxetine

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Medical risk assessment and monitoring for purging: orthostatic vital signs and weight at every visit, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate and creatinine weekly until potassium is normal twice and then at each visit, magnesium and phosphate at baseline and when potassium is low, an ECG at baseline and after any QT-relevant medicine change while potassium is low, and urgent or inpatient care for potassium below 3.0 mmol/L despite replacement, QTc above 500 ms, fainting, a pulse below 50, or blood in the vomit
Eating disorders psychiatry consultation on the diagnosis and its severity, the right level of care, psychological treatment, fluoxetine, and medical monitoring
Oral potassium chloride 20 mEq twice daily, with a recheck in one week; stopped once potassium is normal and vomiting is less frequent
Nutrition: an eating disorders dietitian; regular eating of three meals and two or three snacks a day, no dieting or skipped meals, and no foods banned; caffeine cut down
Dental protection while vomiting continues: no brushing for an hour after vomiting, a non-acid fluoride mouthwash, fewer acidic drinks, and a dental examination
Structured safety assessment, a written safety plan with her warning signs, lethal-means counseling, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, the PHQ-9 at each visit, and safety review at every visit

Eating-disorder-focused cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT-E): 20 sessions over 20 weeks with an eating disorders therapist, twice weekly for the first four weeks, with weighing in session, self-monitoring records, regular eating, work on shape and weight concerns and on binges triggered by difficult feelings, and a written relapse-prevention plan at the end

Fluoxetine started at 20 mg each morning and raised to 40 mg after one week and 60 mg after two weeks, for both the bulimia and the depression; ECG two weeks after reaching 60 mg; mood, sleep, agitation and suicidal thoughts checked at each visit; continued for at least a year after remission
No binge eating or vomiting for at least four weeks by the end of 20 weeks of CBT-E
No binge eating or vomiting for six weeks
Potassium at least 3.5 mmol/L on two checks within four weeks
Regular eating (three meals and two or three snacks) on most days by three months
Regular eating on six or seven days a week
PHQ-9 score below 5 by the end of treatment
EDE-Q global score below 2.0 by the end of treatment

list.item: Independent in all activities; working full time but exhausted in the mornings after evenings of bingeing and vomiting [S]

Examination: lying blood pressure 102/64 and pulse 66; after three minutes standing 98/62 and pulse 88, a rise of 22 per minute, without dizziness; both parotid glands visibly enlarged and non-tender; enamel erosion on the inner surfaces of the upper front teeth; small calluses on the backs of two knuckles of the right hand; no edema; skin intact, no scars of recent self-injury [S]
Alert, articulate, and warm; tearful and ashamed when describing the bingeing and vomiting, and relieved to have said it; thought process organized; no psychotic features; insight good [S]
Mood low, tired, and hopeless about stopping; feels worthless; PHQ-9 14 with item 9 scored 0; no current thoughts of suicide or self-harm [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 1990-02-09: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care with close follow-up. She has no current thoughts of suicide or self-harm and no self-injury now; past self-injury at a time of great distress is part of her history and was discussed with her gently. Eating disorders and depression both raise the risk of suicide and self-harm, so a written safety plan was made with her, with her own warning signs (a run of bad nights of bingeing, feeling hopeless, or wanting to hurt herself) and what to do about each, including whom to call. Lethal-means counseling: no firearm and no access to one; medicines are kept in small amounts. The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) was given and saved in her phone, with the clinic number. Safety reviewed at every visit [S]
